title: Boat excursions, river geography and pilots
summary: Daily trips to Alton, four months in St. Louis and eight in New Orleans, and description of the Ohio and Mississippi, pilots and rapids.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Were these excursions? Yeah. Or just out and down the river? They go up first.

Out of St. Louis, you go up first, Alton, a little past Alton. You see, they go to Alton on the boat in the daytime. And they get up there around two o'clock. They take those people out. They keep the people out about an hour. And the boat comes on back and put those people off. Now, they land in St. Louis at six o'clock. That's every day. The boat was loaded every day. Like today, Monday, Easter Monday, man, that boat was loaded. Monday nights were good, huh? Monday to day. Monday to day, like all the wives and kids and everything. And night was a different crowd. Most had kids and things on Mondays. And I think there was 25 cents for boat ride on the Monday. And they had to turn the people away. That boat hold around five thousand, five hundred and something. And turn them away. They didn't lie over five hundred on that boat, but they used to see down these house. And when they get that big heavy loads, we wouldn't go across them because they had the ticker. They had ticked you. They used to come on. What do you call it? The insurance man, whatever they call it, the front, the gutter man. We'd tick in your car, how many come on. Oh yeah? Well we wouldn't go over that front gang, trying to put a gang plan in the back for all the deck hands. They called it because they called everybody, you know. I see what's in me, yes. See? All the deck hands, your roster, bossy band, see, and the cabin boys, cooks and things. Well we'd go over and slip over that back. Go on, see? Because we'd have a guy up the hill waiting for us there who don't go and tell you what way to go. I see. You stay in St. Louis four months and stay in New Orleans eight. See? Now when you leave St. Louis, down that Mississippi River, you play every town down that river. See? Now when we leave, coming up the boat, see we get out of Ohio, we come up, Liberlo, Kero, Illinois, that Ohio River runs in the Mississippi River, did you know that? Well we run into the Ohio River, that's why we run into Patuco and West Virginia, Hunting, West Virginia. That's right on that Ohio River. Right on up, we run into Patuco, that comes right on up, Cincinnati, Pittsburgh, all up to St. Paul, Minnesota, where the Mississippi, where the Ohio River runs into a- The Mississippi. Yeah. No, it runs in the Mississippi down there. But see, after you pass Pittsburgh, that Ohio River, it stops there. Oh yeah, it runs into the Allegheny or Susquehanna or something like that. Now, now, now, now, then we started going up that Mississippi River all the way to St. Paul, Minnesota, where the Mississippi River emceed into that lake. See? Well I've been to one end of that Mississippi River to the other. Then sometime we'd have a picnic down to what you call the Jettas. That's 141 miles below New Orleans. That's right at the mouthful gulfs of Mexico and the Mississippi River. And they got what you call outlets down there. Outlets where- Where the river embees out? Yeah, embees out. See, Northwest Pass, East West Pass, whatever way you're going, you got to have what you call river pilots, bar pilots, and sea pilots, you know? Uh-huh. Yeah. Yeah. See, you go down there. Now, where you're going, see, and you got to have- you got to pilot house, I don't know where you change pilots when you get on there. What pass? You go in, the big ships come in. Uh-huh. Then they have a river pilot. Then they come up so far in the Mississippi River, then they got to change, see, they go for what they call the bar, the bar pilot. It carries you so far when you leave the gulf down the Jettas, they call it the Jettas. Then he gets off there and the river pilot brings you on in and all in. See? Uh-huh. Now, in Mississippi River, from Kirkwood Highway, you got a rapid pilot to take you in to Davenport Highway. Uh-huh. They got rapids in the middle of the river, some kind of- look like big rocks. They look like a little tombstone right in the middle of the river. Yes. Well, when that water's high, that rapid pilot knows-

Where it is. See? See? Because you like to see a buoy sitting here and one sitting like over there. See? Well, some of those buoys, the boat got to go out in between there. But up in there, the rapids is in between there. Uh-huh. See? And they got to go around.
So you got to know where all those rocks are. Yeah. How long were you with Faith Merrill?
